    CTTIR v5 and project logos

    Source: vignettes/cttir-library.Rmd
    cttir-library.Rmd

    Create first, reuse when useful

    A new project starts with its own name and frame, without an archived motif:

    project <- logo_design("My project", shape = "pentagon")
project <- hex_add_part(project, "circle", x = .5, y = .6, r = .15)
project <- hex_add_part(project, "polygon",
                        x = c(.35, .65, .5), y = c(.45, .45, .75))
hex_layers(project)
#>           id     type    fill     col points  role   name visible
#> 1 layer_0001  polygon #191919 #000000      5 frame  Frame    TRUE
#> 2 layer_0002 pathgrob #FFFFFF    <NA>   1050  name   Name    TRUE
#> 3  part_0001   circle #009E73 #FFFFFF      1 added Circle    TRUE
#> 4  part_0002  polygon #009E73 #FFFFFF      3 added  Shape    TRUE

    Hexagons, regular pentagons and squares share the same object, editing API and export formats. The name is inside the lower part of the frame, and the exterior is transparent. layout = "motif" creates a transparent square without a frame or name. Add primitives there to work from an empty canvas.

    Browse the archive

    The v5 library contains 45 identities. Their 270 original SVG and 270 PDF masters are included unchanged in a compressed archive; hex_asset() returns copies of them and renders the PNG versions from the SVG masters, and the five icon sizes with the package renderer, on demand. Light, dark and monochrome named masters keep the exact package name inside the hex.

    head(hex_catalog())
#>          name        repo   family      symbol      kind
#> 1    molpathR    molpathR clinical    molpathR R package
#> 2      pressR      pressR clinical      pressR R package
#> 3     scimagR     scimagR clinical     scimagR R package
#> 4 zhncommandR zhncommandR clinical zhncommandR R package
#> 5  brainwritR  brainwritR evidence  brainwritR R package
#> 6     delphyr     delphyR evidence     delphyr R package
#>                                                                    source
#> 1                 https://github.com/CTTIR/molpathR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 2                   https://github.com/CTTIR/pressR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 3                  https://github.com/CTTIR/scimagR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 4              https://github.com/CTTIR/zhncommandR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 5               https://github.com/CTTIR/brainwritR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION
#> 6 https://github.com/CTTIR/delphyR/blob/main/packages/delphyr/DESCRIPTION
#>     asset_dir
#> 1    molpathR
#> 2      pressR
#> 3     scimagR
#> 4 zhncommandR
#> 5  brainwritR
#> 6     delphyr

    An explicit identity starts from its editable native R design; original approved assets can be located separately:

    archived <- hex_design("phenoscapR")
print(archived)
hex_asset("phenoscapR", mode = "dark", layout = "lockup", format = "svg")

    hex_design() without an explicit package also starts fresh. For a named project, logo_design("My project") makes that intent explicit. Supply motif = "phenoscapR" only when its full motif should be the starting point; icon = "microscope" instead selects a generic icon.

    Omit layer to import every motif component, excluding the source frame and name:

    project <- hex_reuse_part(project, "phenoscapR")

    The destination keeps its name, frame, palette and existing parts. Each import stores a validated snapshot of native source settings and edits, and remains independently editable. Imported colours therefore stay as chosen in the source until you edit those parts. Changing an archive selection does not alter imported artwork.

    Edit, duplicate and remove 

    project <- hex_edit_layer(project, "part_0001",
                          fill = "#45B59A", dx = .03, scale = .9)
project <- hex_duplicate_part(project, "part_0001")
hex_layers(project)
#>           id     type    fill     col points  role     name visible
#> 1 layer_0001  polygon #191919 #000000      5 frame    Frame    TRUE
#> 2 layer_0002 pathgrob #FFFFFF    <NA>   1050  name     Name    TRUE
#> 3  part_0001   circle #45B59A #FFFFFF      1 added Circle 1    TRUE
#> 4  part_0002  polygon #009E73 #FFFFFF      3 added    Shape    TRUE
#> 5  part_0003    lines #0C4E4B #0C4E4B      7 added     Line    TRUE
#> 6  part_0004   circle #45B59A #FFFFFF      1 added Circle 2    TRUE

    Use current IDs from hex_layers(). Native geometry uses layer_ IDs; additional primitives and imported components use part_ IDs. Adding or removing another part retains the IDs of existing parts.

    hex_edit_layer() accepts fill, outline, line width, opacity, visibility, translation, scale, rotation (angle) and explicit X/Y point coordinates. Coordinates are local to the part’s viewport; supply the same number of points. The input design is unchanged, so keeping an earlier object provides undo in R.

    project <- hex_remove_part(project, "part_0002")

    Removing an added part deletes it. Removing a native part hides it with a saved visibility override. hex_edit_layer(design, id, reset = TRUE) removes that part’s overrides. Review edited scientific shapes at full size and icon size because a changed silhouette can imply a different meaning.

    Portable projects and exports

    Upload local figures and vector artwork with the same project API:

    project <- hex_import_art(project, "figure.svg")  # also PNG or JPEG
project <- hex_label_layer(project, "part_0001", "Central cell")
project <- hex_edit_layer(project, "part_0001", angle = 20, alpha = .8)
hex_groups(project)
project <- hex_group_layers(project, c("part_0001", "part_0002"), "Cells")

    PNG/JPEG becomes one image part with embedded bytes; supported SVG shapes become independently editable vector paths. Neither needs its original file after import. SVG curves use bounded vector polylines. Solid fills/strokes, transforms and local references are supported. Outline text and flatten gradients, masks, filters, group opacity or intersecting clips first; unsupported features produce an error. Uploads are capped at 10 MiB and rasters at 8192 pixels per side and 16 million pixels total. See ?hex_import_art for the complete supported subset and bounds.

    hex_save_design(project, "project.json")
restored <- hex_read_design("project.json")
hex_export(restored, "project.svg")
hex_export(restored, "project.png", width = 1600)
hex_export(restored, "project.pdf")
hex_recipe(restored, "reproduce.R")

    JSON contains only supported settings, geometry and source snapshots. It never loads executable R, external files or serialised grid objects. Unknown fields, nested archive parts, invalid coordinates and projects over 20 MiB are rejected. Earlier v5 JSON files remain supported and retain their archived motif behaviour.

    The bundled JetBrains Mono font supplies outlined name glyphs. Vector exports do not depend on installed fonts. Font licences are supplied under system.file("cttir/source/fonts", package = "hexmakR"). Hex canvases use width/height sqrt(3)/2; pentagon, square and unframed canvases are square.

    Manual editor 

    hexmakr_app()
hexmakr_app(package = "phenoscapR")  # preselect CTTIR Gallery; Designer stays fresh

    The Designer starts with a new logo. Apply its name and frame, add parts, then select, drag and edit individual components. Short labels and editable groups organise the composition. CTTIR Gallery browsing leaves the logo unchanged; adding a selected part, adding a motif, and starting from a whole archive design are separate explicit actions.

    Undo restores applied actions. Reset to starting design returns to the fresh, explicitly loaded archive or opened-project baseline. Save project and Open saved project preserve editable parts. Downloads use the applied design, so apply pending form changes first. The classic workspace remains available as hexmakr_app(workspace = "classic").

    Original catalogue and legacy references 

    # 45 x (2 layouts x 3 modes x 3 formats + 5 icons) = 1,035 exports
hex_render_catalog("exports")

    This regenerates designs from native R geometry. Use hex_asset() when the unchanged approved master is required.

    The twelve names present only in the older hexstickers repository remain legacy SVG references under inst/cttir/legacy in the source repository. They are not claimed as approved v5 motifs. hexmakeR maps to hexmakR; delphyR maps to delphyr.

    CTTIR and cttiR differ only in case. The organisation’s asset directory is CTTIR-brand; the R package retains cttiR. hex_catalog()$asset_dir records this mapping to prevent collisions on macOS and Windows. Display names keep their exact spelling. Archive and asset hashes record the supplied originals.
